chunks.text: 39-year-old male, Professional, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
History of pneumonia resolved 5 years ago
Remote history of fractured right wrist (10 years ago)
Previous use of Omeprazole for GERD, now discontinued
General Anesthesia with Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA) and Ultrasound-Guided Regional Anesthesia (USRA) for postoperative pain management

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Patient's Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go through a few important questions to ensure your safety and comfort during the procedure. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, sure, Doctor. I'm ready to answer your questions.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Let's start with the reason for your surgery. Can you tell me a bit about your symptoms that led to the decision for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Well, Doctor, I've been having a lot of pain in my tummy, especially after eating. The scans showed gallstones, so the doctor said it's best to remove the gallbladder.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. Now, let's move on to your medications. Can you confirm the current list of medications you're taking and any allergies that have been diagnosed since your last medical review?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Okay, so I'm taking Metformin 1000 mg twice daily for my diabetes, Lisinopril 20 mg once daily for blood pressure, and Atorvastatin 40 mg once daily for cholesterol. Oh, and I also started Insulin Glargine 40 units once at night because my sugar levels were a bit high. Oh, and I have an allergy to Penicillin, which I think wasn't recorded before.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for that information. It's important we have the most up-to-date details. So, just to confirm, you're on Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, Insulin Glargine, and you have a Penicillin allergy. Is that correct?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, that's right, Doctor. And the Ranitidine was stopped, as per the doctor's advice.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Now, regarding your NPO status, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, Doctor. I've been fasting as instructed. Just a bit of water with my morning medications, but that was hours ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Have you had any anesthesia before? If so, were there any issues or reactions?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I had a surgery about 5 years ago. I think it was general anesthesia, and everything went smoothly. No problems at all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great to hear. Lastly, how would you describe your overall energy levels and ability to perform daily activities? Are you able to walk up a flight of stairs without getting too breathless?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'd say I'm fairly active, Doctor. I can walk up stairs, but sometimes I get a bit tired, especially if I've eaten a heavy meal. But generally, I manage my daily tasks without too much trouble.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that with me. It helps me understand your fitness for surgery. We'll be using general anesthesia with a Laryngeal Mask Airway and Ultrasound-Guided Regional Anesthesia for your postoperative pain management. Do you have any questions about the anesthesia plan?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, Doctor. You've explained it well. I'm just ready to get this done and feel better.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Very well. If you have any more questions later, don't hesitate to ask. We're here to ensure your surgery and recovery go as smoothly as possible.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate your care.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] LMA size four inserted, good seal, capnograph waveform confirmed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] ultrasound-guided right subcostal transversus abdominis plane block, local anesthetic twenty milligrams of bupivacaine

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] hypotension noted, blood pressure sixty-five over forty, one liter of Ringer's lactate administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] tube in, grade one view, surgery commencing

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:00] normotension maintained, blood pressure one twenty over seventy-five

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm feeling okay, a bit tired but not in too much pain.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Can you tell me your pain level on a scale from 0 to 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 3 or 4, it's manageable.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or feeling like you might vomit?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I feel fine, no sickness at all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. How's your breathing? Any discomfort or tightness in your chest?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine, no problem there.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Did you experience any awareness or discomfort during the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't remember anything, slept through it all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Given your diabetes and high blood pressure, are you having any dizziness or vision changes?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, everything looks and feels normal to me.

Current medications include Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, and Insulin Glargine. No known drug allergies except for the newly reported Penicillin allergy.

Intraoperative course included induction with Propofol, LMA insertion, and ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia for postoperative pain management. Hypotension was noted and managed with fluid resuscitation.
Normotension was restored and maintained. Surgery commenced with a grade one view after tube placement.
Monitor for postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) due to general anesthesia and history of GERD. Be cautious of airway compromise due to LMA use in a patient with GERD history.
Watch for hypoglycemia due to insulin use and intraoperative NPO status. Manage hypertension postoperatively given the patient's chronic condition.
Anticipate potential pain management challenges due to regional anesthesia and possible breakthrough pain. Be prepared for delayed recovery due to Propofol use for induction.
Continue to monitor for hemodynamic instability post-induction due to intraoperative hypotension.
